```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  dev.args = list(bg = "white"),
  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4
)
```

```{r setup}
library(tidydiversity)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
set.seed(42)
```

The examples use `png_ants`: ants recorded at nutrient baits along the
Mt Wilhelm elevational gradient in Papua New Guinea, in the dry and wet
seasons (Moses et al. 2023). Each bait at which a species was found counts
as one occurrence.

## Hill numbers

Hill numbers express diversity as an effective number of species. Order
`q = 0` is richness, `q = 1` weights species by their frequency and
`q = 2` emphasises the dominant species.

```{r}
div_hill(png_ants, q = c(0, 1, 2), .by = season)
```

## Sample coverage

Raw counts depend on sampling effort. Sample coverage estimates how
complete each sample is.

```{r}
div_coverage(png_ants, .by = season)
```

## Asymptotic estimates

`div_estimate()` gives Chao1 richness, the Chao et al. (2013) Shannon
estimator and the unbiased Simpson estimator, with bootstrap intervals.

```{r}
div_estimate(png_ants, .by = season, nboot = 50) |>
  filter(q == 0)
```

## Rarefaction and extrapolation

`div_rarefy()` interpolates each sample down to smaller sizes and
extrapolates up to twice its size. The values match the iNEXT package.

```{r}
curves <- png_ants |>
  filter(season == "wet") |>
  div_rarefy(q = c(0, 1, 2), nboot = 30)
curves
```

```{r, fig.alt = "Rarefaction and extrapolation curves for each site"}
autoplot(curves)
```

Plotting against coverage shows how complete each sample is:

```{r, fig.alt = "Diversity plotted against sample coverage"}
autoplot(curves, x = "coverage")
```

## Fair comparisons

Compare sites at equal completeness with `div_standardise()`. With no level
given, each group is standardised to the lowest coverage that its sites
reach at twice their sample size.

```{r}
std <- div_standardise(png_ants, .by = season, nboot = 50)
std
```

```{r, fig.alt = "Coverage-standardised richness by elevation"}
std |>
  left_join(distinct(png_ants, site, elevation), by = "site") |>
  filter(q == 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(elevation, diversity, colour = season)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Elevation (m)", y = "Richness at equal coverage") +
  scale_colour_tidydiversity() +
  theme_tidydiversity()
```
